description:
Today, SPY tested lower band VWAP (yellow line on 1st attached image) after rejecting the VWAP (purple line on 1st attached image) at open. Lower band VWAP turned out to be the support zone and price started to increase beyond VWAP (open level). After the price surpassed VWAP I entered SPX 7810Cs, anticipating a breakout above upper band VWAP (purple line on 1st attached image), (SPY chart; SPX chart lacks volume statistic indicators like VWAP). However, the breakout wasn't strong enough for me to hold. After 7810Cs chopped between VWAP and upper band VWAP. I re-entered 7810Cs again expecting that it would surpass the upper band VWAP on this double bottom. However, 7810Cs made a third pull back before a breakout, making me exit the position for breakeven. No put side were traded today during the reversal towards EOD.

15 fills; 1min 50sec; 50 sec scalps

Today, the S&P 500 continued to chop down and tested the trend line again on my weekly chart (reference 2nd image). This trend line started at the 2022 trend reversal, as shown in the image. It has been an efficient price magnet for couple weeks now.

 "Market is neither efficient nor random. Market is not efficient because there are too many poorly conceived opinions, and it is not random because strong investor emotions create what we call a trend." 

No trades today.

When ES was at +0.13% I entered a long position (2 lots) at 7881.50 (yesterday 3:30 pm PST). I got stopped out for 47pts total for both contracts overnight and around 2:30am PST I switched to a short position (2 lots) when the S&P 500 futures hit -0.22%. 

I got out of that position at the open drop for a total of 50pts, ending the day at +3 pts. I did not make any additional trades throughout the day as I expected a 4-hour MACD continuation into today instead of this overnight drop.

3pts; 2 round turns

I didn't really trade today as there were no visible setups in my favor. Only made a 5-sec scalp trade last minute before the close for 16%, with just 1 contract.

It is so important to show up every market day and learn to stare at the chart without taking a trade. I can’t emphasize enough how important it is to show up. As full time traders, we are just merely managing the risk of our portfolio everyday. In the market everyone is competing against Warren Buffett to hedge fund managers to private traders like us who sits in front of our computer literally +80hours weekly staring at the tape/thinking about the market even though actual trades/scalps take minutes. It’s important to comprehend that 95% lose money in the market and among those profitable 5%, 99% are active traders, meaning they trade almost everyday. “Trading is hard” is an understatement because most will lose everything and there’s no guarantee you will be profitable in the future. Real traders would understand how much the market breaks you; your ego, your illusions of control, your sense of certainty and tests your worst. How you question yourself, your process, and your future more times than you want to admit. However, if you are a trader you will come back and show up for the market everyday. You really got to love it and that’s what defines a trader. There is an ancient Arabic saying: a group of sheep led by one lion will beat a group of lions led by one sheep. Become a lion in the market.

2 fills; 5sec scalp

I entered a short position at 7831 around 4:58 pm PST yesterday, got stopped out overnight at 7846 for 30pts. I made several long scalps at open on the way up and short position on the first pull back, managed to recover to +2 pts for the day. Then during the reversal, I did enter couple short positions but got stopped out due to tight stops. I was hoping for a continuation after breaking the VWAP but it stayed choppy towards the close. Frustrating day as my positions were hitting stops every time I moved it down for a point or two to secure profit. Gave up what I recovered during the morning scalps from those little chops, ended the day back at -30pts. Definitely overtraded today.

-30 pts; +30 round turns

Today, market had a decent overnight move up and the trend continued for another 2 hours after open. I entered 7850Cs as the market started to breakout after the market-open chop. Scalped twice for 7%-8%. During the reversal, I scalped 7800Ps for 7%. It felt like a day manipulated by the institutions; on 1-min chart (consecutive small candles followed by one huge opposing candle to flatten out the price). I think the price will likely hold until the midterms.

17 fills; 1min 12sec; 10sec; 24sec scalps

I entered a long position (2 lots) last night around 5 pm PST (Sunday), but the market reversed overnight so /ES stayed red until hour before the open. Therefore, I decided to close my position for breakeven shortly after open during the pump. I closed the long position around 6:32am PST for +2 pts. Then it broke out, scalped some calls on the way, but I did not feel comfortable with my entries and felt like I missed the move after closing my overnight longs. Did not enter anything to hold throughout the day; just entered a short position towards EOD during the reversal. Moved my stop down to secure profit at the top of 2nd to last 5-min candle before close.

14pts; 7 round turns

Today was a trend day. However, 7780Cs did not break out until later in the day. I did not hold as the relative 3-day volume was around 85%, on a low volume trend day reversal can easily happen, but these contracts ended up breaking out to around $15k (10/contracts) towards eod. Still expired worthless though.

18 fills; all less than 1-min scalps
